record.title: halo puck — the vertical stack budget as space claims (lane M, mechanical)
record.frame_convention: origin ON THE AXIS OF REVOLUTION at the lowest point of the battery door's outer face — Apple's own drawing datum (research/fetched/G-airtag-profile-from-dxf.md); +z up toward the crown apex at z=7.98; +x through the 6 o'clock bayonet ledge, so the three ledges sit at 0/120/240 deg (= 6, 10 and 2 o'clock, DECISIONS.md D13); millimetres. halo is a CONCENTRIC product, so every box below is a Z-SLAB of the 7.98 mm stack budget and its dx=dy is the diameter of the WIDEST occupant of that slab; a cuboid claim cannot express a ring, and two concentric parts at the same height always share a bounding box, so the radial budget is carried in must_provide and purpose instead

boxes.name: door-skin
boxes.purpose: the stamped 301 stainless battery door: 0.30 mm skin at the axis, outer face an R92 spherical cap that IS the z datum, Ø25.44 at z=0.88, Ø25.55 wall to z=1.89, three Ø27.84 bayonet tabs at z 1.89..2.19. The only user-openable part (SPEC F12)

interfaces_to_siblings.where: the door's inner face is the cell's seat

constraints.notes: 0.30 mm is halo's choice, not a measurement: lane G records the AirTag cover thickness as 'estimate, unverified' (research/07 §5.2 row 1). A donor sample settles it.

boxes.name: door-dome-dead-air
boxes.purpose: dead air: the sagitta of the R92 dome under the cell's Ø19.6 contact circle. 19.6^2/(8*92) = 0.522 mm. This is the design's only reclaimable slack — emboss a flat pad in the door and 0.52 mm comes back

constraints.notes: 0.542 mm is READ OFF Apple's own ordinate table at the cell's Ø20.00 RIM. Seating the cell on a smaller circle (19.60) put 0.134 mm3 of cell inside the door — the interference check measured it

boxes.name: cr2032
boxes.purpose: the CR2032 cell, Ø20.0 x 3.2 mm, positive face DOWN onto the door's inner dome, negative face UP to the sprung fingers. 40% of the whole height budget in one part

constraints.notes: at the same height, radially outboard: the door's Ø25.55 wall (r 12.475..12.775), the carrier's Ø24.75 seal land with its O-ring, the three bayonet ledges (Ø25.90..27.90) and the shell skirt above z=2.29. A cuboid box cannot claim a ring, so they are named here rather than boxed

boxes.name: battery-contacts
boxes.purpose: three formed C5191 phosphor-bronze fingers, 0.15 mm stock, at their COMPRESSED height. Two positive on the can rim at r 9.5, one negative on the cell's negative face at r 6.0 (Catley: 2 positive + 1 negative, all on the carrier side). No coin-cell holder fits — the lowest-profile retainer is 2 mm (lane G)

interfaces_to_siblings.where: the fingers clamp the cell down onto the door

constraints.notes: the slab is the 0.100 mm embossed contact dimple plus the 0.150 mm C5191 stock, measured off the built finger; the free tip sits DEFLECT_NOM=0.400 mm lower and the door's detent asks for 0.250 mm more

boxes.name: carrier-pcb-seat
boxes.purpose: the LDS carrier's working section: the three insert-moulded finger roots, their tails up to pads on the board's underside, and the annular PCB seat at z=4.600. The carrier also owns the Ø23.11 seal land, the O-ring groove and the three bayonet ledges lower down, and carries the BLE/NFC/UWB LDS antenna traces on its Ø27.40 outer wall

constraints.notes: no metal in the part: the only conductors are the LDS traces (which ARE the antennas) and the insert-moulded fingers. No fastener, no shield, no stiffener anywhere inside Apple's Ø37.31 antenna keep-out

boxes.name: pcb
boxes.purpose: the 4-layer board, Ø26.0 x 0.60 mm, with three 26 deg notches at 0/120/240 deg (iFixit's 'three notches made for the clips that hold the tag together'). Apple's is 0.30 mm and 'likely to be damaged when removed'; 0.60 mm is far cheaper to fabricate and the height is available once Apple's voice-coil motor is deleted

boxes.name: pcb-top-components
boxes.purpose: top-side component allowance: 0.40 mm inside Ø21.2 (under the bender), 1.60 mm outboard of it. Everything tall — the five 100 uF bulk caps, the crystals — goes on the BOTTOM face, into the 3.4 mm annulus outboard of the cell

boxes.name: diaphragm-gap
boxes.purpose: the moving gap. This IS Apple's Ø25.75 'DO NOT OBSTRUCT THIS AREA' callout expressed as a volume, and NOTHING may enter it — not the carrier, not the board, not a component. It is what lets the bender drive the crown

boxes.name: piezo-bender
boxes.purpose: Murata 7BB-20-3 bare piezo bender, Ø20.0 x 0.22 mm, 3.6 kHz, 500 ohm (DECISIONS.md D11a), plus a 0.05 mm structural bond line to the shell's FLAT internal land. Driven anti-phase from two SoC pins — no boost, no inductor

interfaces_to_siblings.where: bonded full-face to the flat land; the bond is the acoustic coupling

boxes.name: crown-wall
boxes.purpose: the PC crown, which IS the diaphragm (Apple's trick, done with a catalogue part). 1.430 mm at the axis falling to 0.800 mm at the land edge Ø21.4, because the INSIDE is a flat land at z=6.550 while the outside keeps Apple's R92 cap. Flat because conforming a 7BB-20-3 to R91.2 strains its PZT to 0.138%, past the ~0.1% tensile limit of hard PZT
